item.title: U.S. and Iran trade strikes for the first time in a month
item.description: Iran says it targeted U.S. bases in Jordan after CENTCOM announced strikes on rocket launchers on an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: 1 dead, around 15 missing as Grand Canyon hit by flash floods
item.description: The flash floods hit Bright Angel Canyon and the Phantom Ranch area on Saturday afternoon, the National Park Service said.

item.title: Nepal on high alert for fresh flooding as death toll rises past 900
item.description: More than 3,000 people are still missing after catastrophic flash floods hit following a glacial collapse high in the Himalayan region.

item.title: U.S. military strikes Iranian targets in first military action in a month
item.description: As the war passes the six-month mark, neither side showed any sign of backing down.

item.title: Nicolás Maduro shares photos from New York prison: "We are standing firm"
item.description: In the two photographs, Venezuela's deposed leader Nicolás Maduro is wearing a gray tracksuit and making peace signs with his hands.

item.title: ICE sends Afghans and others to Africa, expanding "third country" deportations
item.description: Over a 10-day period, the Trump administration sent more than 100 deportees from Afghanistan, Cuba and other nations to eight countries across Africa, according to internal government documents obtained by CBS News.

item.title: Youth program teaches tennis, academics for the "skills to be champions in life"
item.description: The U.S. Open officially began on Sunday, but the tournament is just one reason a record number of Americans are picking up a racket. Jarred Hill reports on the Harlem Junior Tennis and Education Program, helping young players succeed on the court and beyond.

item.title: Roman Space Telescope promises 300-megapixel views of the cosmos
item.description: The $4.3 billion telescope is expected to discover tens of thousands of exoplanets while probing the nature of mysterious dark matter and energy.

item.title: NASA launches its Roman Space Telescope to explore the hidden universe
item.description: NASA's Roman Space Telescope​ launched shortly after daybreak from Kennedy Space Center and blazed toward an observation point 1 million miles away.

item.title: A look at NASA's Roman Space Telescope, heading into deep space
item.description: NASA's next-generation telescope blasted off atop a SpaceX rocket at the Kennedy Space Center on Sunday. The $4.3 billion Roman Space Telescope is on a journey to peer at distant stars and galaxies. Mark Strassmann has more about what some call "the discovery machine."

item.title: Connecticut senator says ICE made arrests at school bus stops, border czar rejects claim
item.description: White House border czar Tom Homan rejected claims that ICE officers arrest parents at bus stops in Connecticut. But there is no argument that arrests are up nationwide. Lana Zak reports from Stamford, Connecticut.

item.title: Israeli settlers attack NBC News crew, Palestinian woman in West Bank
item.description: An NBC News crew was in a Palestinian village in the West Bank when they were attacked by Israeli settlers over the weekend. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemned the incident. Leigh Kiniry reports.

item.title: Trump says U.S. deal with Venezuela will boost oil reserves
item.description: President Trump said the U.S. will begin "topping out" its strategic petroleum reserve with Venezuelan oil under last week's agreement. But that's unlikely to provide much relief to Americans facing sustained high gas prices. Olivia Gazis has more details on the unprecedented agreement.

item.title: Several missing, dozens evacuated amid sudden Grand Canyon flooding
item.description: Dozens of people have been evacuated after sudden flash flooding struck the Grand Canyon. Torrents of water raced through, washing out footbridges over a creek that leads to the Colorado River. The National Park Service said approximately 15 people are missing or unaccounted for. Andrew Kozak has more.

item.title: Nepal on alert for new flooding, death toll passes 800
item.description: The river in Nepal that surged like a tsunami from the high Himalayas surged again on Sunday, this time from torrential rains this wet season. Thousands of people are still missing after the devastating floods last week. Ramy Inocencio reports.

item.title: 2 dead, 8 wounded in Trenton shooting, prosecutor says
item.description: Two people died and eight others were hurt in a shooting on Locust Street in Trenton early Sunday morning, officials say.

item.title: Ross Fire burns 85,000 acres, leaves destruction across 2 counties
item.description: The Ross wildfire has burned more than 80,000 acres across Palo Pinto and Jack counties, forcing evacuations, closing roads and disrupting schools.

item.title: The Kanneh-Mason family: Meet the 7 siblings playing classical music | 60 Minutes
item.description: The Kanneh-Mason family boasts seven classically trained musicians, each under the age of 30. The siblings have toured the world and recorded chart-topping albums.

item.title: Remembering the Cap Arcona: Nazi ship sunk with concentration camp prisoners on board
item.description: The Cap Arcona, a Nazi ship, was attacked by British Royal Air Force planes near the end of World War II. Thousands of prisoners died as the ship sank in the horrific and little-known disaster.

item.description: First, a report on the sinking of the Cap Arcona Nazi ship. Then, the Kanneh-Masons: Meet the musical siblings.

item.title: 8/30: CBS Weekend News
item.description: Nepal warns of new flooding amid ongoing devastation; President Trump says the oil deal with Venezuela will boost U.S. oil reserves.

item.title: Google updates maps to show "Lake America" in U.S. after Trump order
item.description: Google announced that it had begun rolling out changes to how its maps display Lake Ontario's name, after President Trump signed an executive order changing it to "Lake America."

item.title: Indianapolis Colts player Keenan Allen arrested on drunken driving charges
item.description: Keenan Allen, a longtime NFL player who recently signed with the Indianapolis Colts, was arrested early Sunday for operating a motor vehicle while intoxicated, police said.

item.title: John James, GOP governor candidate, says tariffs can't "be borne on the backs of Michiganders"
item.description: Amid the trade war between Canada and the U.S. that will likely affect Michigan and the auto industry, Rep. John James, the Republican candidate for governor in Michigan, told "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" that he has been in contact with members of the trade team because "it cannot be borne on the backs of Michiganders."

item.title: Nepal flash flood death toll reaches 800, with around 3,000 still missing
item.description: Poor weather and challenging terrain have hampered aerial rescue operations in Nepal and Tibet.

item.title: Abdul El-Sayed apologizes for his comments about Michigan synagogue attack
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Michigan, has apologized to the state's Jewish Democratic Caucus.

item.title: 8/29: CBS Weekend News
item.description: Trump says gas prices to fall with new deal; Iran war hikes diesel costs for school buses.

item.title: Trump cannot deport students for criticizing Israel, federal judge rules
item.description: The judge delivered a victory for Stanford University's student newspaper, which said some international students were afraid to speak out because of the deportation threat.
